---
title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Six common graphs in cleanplots and in Stata's traditional scheme s2color"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

Each example below, except the last, draws the same graph twice: once with
`scheme(cleanplots)` and once with `scheme(s2color)`, Stata's traditional
scheme. Nothing else about the commands changes. Each
example loads its data from the web, so every example can be run as shown.
With `set scheme cleanplots, perm` in place, the `scheme()` option is not
needed.

## Histogram

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/addhealth4", clear

hist vidtv, percent scheme(cleanplots)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-hist-cleanplots.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do>>
hist vidtv, percent scheme(s2color)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-hist-s2color.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![cleanplots](fig/ex-hist-cleanplots.png){fig-alt="Histogram of hours of video and television per week with the cleanplots scheme: white background, light gridlines, horizontal axis labels."}

![s2color](fig/ex-hist-s2color.png){fig-alt="The same histogram in the s2color scheme."}
:::

## Predictions from an ordinal logit with dashed confidence intervals

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
quietly ologit health orole vrole i.woman age income i.race i.educ
quietly margins, at(orole=(0(1)10))

marginsplot, recastci(rline) ciopts(lpattern(dash) color(*.5)) scheme(cleanplots) ///
    legend(order(6 "Poor" 7 "Fair" 8 "Good" 9 "Very Good" 10 "Excellent"))
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-ologit-cleanplots.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do>>
marginsplot, recastci(rline) ciopts(lpattern(dash) color(*.5)) scheme(s2color) ///
    legend(order(6 "Poor" 7 "Fair" 8 "Good" 9 "Very Good" 10 "Excellent"))
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-ologit-s2color.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![cleanplots](fig/ex-ologit-cleanplots.png){fig-alt="Predicted probabilities of five self-rated health categories across a count of obligatory roles, with dashed confidence-interval lines, in the cleanplots scheme: each category has its own color, marker, and line pattern."}

![s2color](fig/ex-ologit-s2color.png){fig-alt="The same plot in the s2color scheme."}
:::

## Predictions at combinations of two nominal variables

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
quietly logit alcB i.woman##i.parrole c.age i.race i.educ c.wages
quietly margins, at(woman=(0 1) educ=(0(1)4))

marginsplot, recast(scatter) x(educ) scheme(cleanplots)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-pred-cleanplots.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do>>
marginsplot, recast(scatter) x(educ) scheme(s2color)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-pred-s2color.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![cleanplots](fig/ex-pred-cleanplots.png){fig-alt="Predicted probability of drinking alcohol by education level for men and women, as points with confidence intervals, in the cleanplots scheme."}

![s2color](fig/ex-pred-s2color.png){fig-alt="The same plot in the s2color scheme."}
:::

## Bar chart

`cleanplots` uses its softer palette for the bars.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss", clear

graph bar income, over(degree) over(woman) asyvars scheme(cleanplots)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-bar-cleanplots.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do>>
graph bar income, over(degree) over(woman) asyvars scheme(s2color)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-bar-s2color.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![cleanplots](fig/ex-bar-cleanplots.png){fig-alt="Bar chart of mean income by degree, grouped by gender, in the cleanplots scheme: softer bar colors and a light grid."}

![s2color](fig/ex-bar-s2color.png){fig-alt="The same bar chart in the s2color scheme."}
:::

## Residual and influence plot

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/pew16", clear

quietly logit trump i.woman c.age ib4.educ i.race i.polparty3 ///
              i.religB c.income ib3.region
gen index = _n
predict residstd, rs
predict influence, dbeta

twoway scatter residstd index [w=influence], scheme(cleanplots)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-resid-cleanplots.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do>>
twoway scatter residstd index [w=influence], scheme(s2color)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-resid-s2color.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![cleanplots](fig/ex-resid-cleanplots.png){fig-alt="Scatter plot of standardized residuals against observation number with markers sized by influence, in the cleanplots scheme."}

![s2color](fig/ex-resid-s2color.png){fig-alt="The same plot in the s2color scheme."}
:::

## Lowess plot

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/scireview3", clear
sort phd

lowess jobimp phd, scheme(cleanplots)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-lowess-cleanplots.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do>>
lowess jobimp phd, scheme(s2color)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-lowess-s2color.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![cleanplots](fig/ex-lowess-cleanplots.png){fig-alt="Lowess smoother of job importance against PhD prestige with the scatter of points, in the cleanplots scheme."}

![s2color](fig/ex-lowess-s2color.png){fig-alt="The same lowess plot in the s2color scheme."}
:::

## All ten colors

A scatter plot with ten groups and the matching bar chart show the full
palette, with the darker and lighter colors alternating.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss", clear
keep if year == 2016

twoway scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 1, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 2, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 3, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 4, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 5, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 7, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 8, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 9, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 10, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       scatter income occprest if isco88cat == 11, msize(medium) jitter(10) || ///
       , scheme(cleanplots) ///
       legend(order(1 "higher controllers" 2 "lo controllers" 3 "routine nonmanual" ///
              4 "sempl with emp" 5 "sempl without empl" 6 "manual supervisor" ///
              7 "skilled manual" 8 "semi-unskilld manual" 9 "farm labor" ///
              10 "selfempl farm"))
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-ten-scatter-cleanplots.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do>>
graph bar income, over(isco88cat) asyvars scheme(cleanplots) ///
    title("Average income by occupation")
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/ex-ten-bar-cleanplots.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Scatter plot](fig/ex-ten-scatter-cleanplots.png){fig-alt="Scatter plot of income against occupational prestige with ten occupation groups in the ten cleanplots colors and marker symbols."}

![Bar chart](fig/ex-ten-bar-cleanplots.png){fig-alt="Bar chart of average income for ten occupation groups in the softer cleanplots bar colors."}
:::
